name: Twilight Group War Lords
reason: 'War Lord' renders the source rank 'War Reverend' (heavily used in the aligned chapters 620-669), and the 'Twilight Group' localizes the source Night Clan faction; the compound names that group's War Reverend-rank fighters.
description: A squad of four War Reverend-level fighters attached to the Twilight Group during the expedition arc (Eps 645-680). They fight alongside Malcolm, Timothy and Shane against the demonic hordes and are ultimately wiped out in Ep 680.

name: Divine Emperor’s Secret Land
issues: Name drift: Eps 792-838 call it the 'Divine Emperor's Secret Realm' while Eps 854+ use 'Divine Emperor's Secret Land' for the same location.
reason: Source term 'Divine Emperor Secret Realm' was carried over nearly literally, with 'Secret Land' as the settled later-episode form.
description: One of the four hidden lands of the Sacred Feather Sea, a looming black island radiating oppressive energy (Ep 889). It is a vast, perfectly preserved graveyard holding the dragon-blooded corpses, and can only be entered and navigated by souls merged with Soul Cores.

name: Soul Purifying Light
reason: The source's English term 'Soul Purifying Light' (also rendered 'Soul Cleansing Light' in chapters 868-872) was kept as-is for the adaptation.
description: A deadly purifying light encountered during the tower climb (Eps 891-895) that even powerful souls cannot withstand; Zane and the Soul Sea warriors must carefully time their movements to avoid it as it sweeps across the stairs.

name: Path of Heroes
reason: The source term 'Saint's Road' was renamed 'Path of Heroes' to fit the Western fantasy register of the adaptation.
description: A perilous road across the Sacred Feather Sea (Eps 904-926) that travelers traverse under cover of giant shields against incoming attacks; in Ep 908 it becomes a vertical road descending into a vast cylindrical abyss.

name: Barrett
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Barrett' was chosen as a solid, craftsman-like name for the legendary weaponsmith Che Daozi, whose auctioned manual 'Weapon Refining Ancestral Techniques' became 'Barrett's Principles of Forging'.
description: The Capital's legendary Master Weaponsmith, who died two years before Ep 98. His personal journal, the Principles of Forging, holds a lifetime of his techniques and secrets and fetches enormous sums at auction (Eps 98-143).

name: Energy Capsule
reason: No direct source term is evidenced; the adaptation re-packages the source's consumable cultivation aids as graded, crystalline 'Energy Capsules' to suit its Western fantasy register (MasterLS: NOT 'Energy Potion').
description: Graded consumable capsules of crystalline appearance (Grade-two ones gleam with azure light, Ep 96) that boost a cultivator's power. Inner Disciples receive monthly allocations, and Great Houses commonly use them as a shortcut to inflate their scions' power levels without real combat experience (Ep 90).

name: Wyvern
reason: The source's 'Five-Clawed Black Dragon' energy construct was re-imagined as an 'Armored Wyvern', likely to avoid overlap with the show's other dragon entities (e.g. the Cobalt Dragon).
description: A devouring energy construct Zane commands during the battle at Eps 139-140; it swallows enemy constructs such as the Apex Dragon and gleaming swords whole, swelling to more than double its size with each attack it consumes.

name: Vitality Avatar
reason: Since the show renders the source energy 'Zhen Yuan/True Essence' as 'Vitality', the source's 'True Essence avatar' became 'Vitality Avatar'.
description: A manifestation of a warrior's Vitality created through meditation on one's cultivation method; per Saul (Eps 161-175), avatars formed without a Contemplation Picture are 'flimsy', which is why Eastern Territory warriors lag behind others at the same level.

name: Armored Warrior
reason: The source's unnamed 'armored soldier' opponent was kept as a descriptive label, upgraded to 'Armored Warrior' for the adaptation.
description: An unnamed armored opponent Zane grapples with during the trial fight of Eps 163-164; he shapes Raw Vitality into arcs of light and uses slippery, snake-like grappling (the 'Serpent's Coil'), mirroring the armored soldier who slid down Luo Zheng's arm like a snake in the source.

name: Demon Purge
reason: An event name coined by the adaptation for the sect's campaign against the demons (the source's demon-war arc around White Emperor City); no matching source event name appears in the evidence.
description: The sect's campaign/trial against the demons in which Zane and other acolytes took part; after it ended it is used as a time reference for characters' whereabouts (Eps 168-247).

name: Mount Judgment
reason: The source sect's disciplinary 'Admonition Hall' was localized as Mount Judgment and its Hall of Judgment, reframing the institution as a judiciary peak of the Sect.
description: The Sect's disciplinary peak, home to the Hall of Judgment that interrogates rule-breaking acolytes using methods copied from the Empire's imperial judgment halls. Per the records, it had not always held so much power, growing in authority as the Sect expanded (Eps 168-189).

name: Steward Carter
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name: source 'Deacon Cao' (the Blue Cloud Sect deacon guarding the Illusory Fish Pond) became 'Steward Carter', echoing the 'C' surname and keeping his functionary title.
description: The Skyreach Sect's steward of Emberfin Lake (Eps 183-184), a nervous functionary caught between powerful disciples squabbling over the fishing spots. Like the source's Deacon Cao, he resurfaces much later in a demoted patrol role (Eps ~947-971).

name: Mythic-grade
reason: Adjectival form of the canonical tier-3 'Mythic Weapon' grade.

name: Soulbound Weapon
issues: Possible split/early drift: Eps 21-24 use 'Soulbound Weapon' for the source's supreme 'Spiritual Weapon' treasure class, while the show's canonical weapon tiers use 'Spirit Weapon' (tier 2) for the related source term.
reason: The source's 'Spiritual Weapon' - the most valuable treasure class, which clans would war over - was rendered 'Soulbound Weapon' in the early episode batch.
description: A legendary class of artifacts bordering on the mythical, so valuable that wars were fought over mere rumors of their existence and every great house vied for one (Ep 21). Zane suspects he may have unknowingly forged one in Ep 24.

name: Infusion
reason: An adaptation term for the final stage of weaponsmithing; no matching source term for this named step appears in the evidence.
description: The final, most sacred step in weaponsmithing: the moment a craftsman pours their profound understanding into a weapon, bestowing it with a grade and purpose (Ep 216). It can also be performed on an existing blade rather than a fresh forging (Ep 214).

name: Benjamin
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Benjamin' echoes the source given name 'Bin' of Long Bin, the big poison-wielding competitor with a blood-red broadsword.
description: A big, imposing cultivator and minor opponent at the competition (Eps 235-236). A poison specialist (Creeping Blight Venom, mirroring Long Bin's Blood River Chariot poison) who wields a scarlet machete, he is unsettled and defeated by the gentle-looking Jill and her diminutive Emerald Sword.

name: Top One Hundred
reason: Source term 'top 100' (the elite bracket of the sect's All-Peak Competition rankings) was carried over as 'Top One Hundred'.
description: The elite top-hundred bracket of the sect's grand competition rankings, which determines the standing of the peaks. Breaking into it at only the Second Level of the Adept Realm, as Jacob did (source: Wang Yun), was considered an incredible record (Eps 246-286).

name: Shadow Group
issues: MasterLS calls it the 'Skyreach Sect's secretive assassin division', but the episodes (Ep 273+) describe an independent ancient assassin bloodline dismantled 300 years ago by the Burning Sky Dynasty, the Skyreach Sect and the Seven Great Houses - the MasterLS note is inaccurate.
reason: The source's 'Shadow Clan' - the assassin clan that killed emperors and threatened the Fentian Dynasty and the Seven Major Noble Clans - was localized as the 'Shadow Group'.
description: An ancient assassin bloodline that once terrorized the Eastern Territory and claimed the lives of emperors. Its local branch was dismantled three hundred years ago by the Burning Sky Dynasty, the Skyreach Sect and the Seven Great Houses, but the still-wealthy organization survives elsewhere and has poured its fortune into Johanson, its first true prodigy in three centuries (Eps 273-634).

name: Life-Essence
issues: Possible term overlap: the show's canon uses 'Life Energy' (below Nature Level) and 'Life Force' (Nature Level+); 'Life-Essence' appears sporadically (Eps 284-1038) as a third variant for a cultivator's fundamental life power.
reason: A rendering of the source's generic life-essence/vital-origin concept that cultivators burn or pour into artifacts; no single source term is pinned by the evidence.
description: A cultivator's fundamental life power, which can be expended or sacrificed to fuel techniques and artifacts; in Ep 1038 Fenton pours his own Life-Essence into his Law-forged Painting, staining its golden state with a bloody aura.

name: Soul-Illuminated Realm
issues: MasterLS marks this realm as new world-building content, but Ep 461 ('a third-grade Soul-Illuminated Realm cultivator') directly parallels source Ch ~448 ('a Third Level Divine Reflection Realm warrior') - it localizes an existing source realm rather than inventing one.
reason: The source cultivation realm 'Divine Reflection Realm' (literally 'illuminating the divine/soul') was localized as the 'Soul-Illuminated Realm'.
description: A cultivation realm above the Soul Realm, divided into numbered grades (third and fourth grades are cited in Eps 461 and 485). Used between Eps 296-485 for cultivators at the stage the source calls the Divine Reflection Realm.

name: Sword Tempering Pool
reason: The source term 'Sword Cleansing Pool' was renamed 'Sword Tempering Pool' to fit the Western fantasy register of the adaptation.
description: A lesser hallowed ground, per the ancient tomes (Ep 358), into which a swordsman is pulled upon grasping the Apex of Sword Intent. Finn trained there after his breakthrough, sharpening his skills and merging thunderbolts with his sword intent (Eps 303-356).

name: Elder Toby
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name: the source's Cloud Hall Deacon/Elder Xiao (who runs the card draws at the conference, Ch ~473) became 'Elder Toby'.
description: A Cloud Hall elder (Eps 358-733) who administers the card-drawing rules at the martial conference (Ep 487) and frets over explaining Frank's disappearance to Frank's father Emanuel, while prudently staying on good terms with the rising Zane.

name: Red Fire Snake
reason: The source creature 'Scarlet Fire Snake' was lightly renamed 'Red Fire Snake' for the adaptation.
description: An enormous lava-dwelling serpent encountered during the trial (Eps 361-372); it lunges from the lava at disciples, and Zane's dodge leaves the enraged creature for the four disciples behind him to handle.

name: Tier-Two Sect
reason: The source's numeric sect grading ('second grade sect') was rendered as 'Tier-Two Sect' for the Western fantasy setting.
description: A rank in the continent's sect hierarchy below the great factions; the Skyreach Sect is a Tier-Two sect (Ep 427), and students from Tier-Two sects defer to holders of a Cloud Hall Token (Ep 408).

name: Exterminating Wheel
reason: The source's 'Wheel of Death' - the rudimentary first form of the Demon Blood Emperor's 'Ten Thousand Fiend Karmic Wheel' - was renamed the 'Exterminating Wheel'.
description: The first level of a technique Zane cultivates by drawing on Malice (Ep 409): a wheel construct that spins at terrifying speed and can suck in and lock onto whatever passes through it, as when it seized Frank's spear rather than his body (Ep 412).

name: Marcus
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Marcus' was chosen for Zhuo Feiling, Zhuo Bufan's (Frank's) older and stronger brother, a ninth-stage spear expert.
description: Frank's elder brother and a formidable spear user who wields a blood-red spear (the source's Zhuo Feiling with his Annihilation Spear). He confronts Zane over Frank's humiliation (Eps 411-414), unaware that he is really fighting Saint Morphen, whose Fusion Realm puppetry channels power directly through Zane's body.

name: Chris Fane
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name; the surname 'Fane' echoes the source family name 'Fang', keeping House Fane as a consistent family unit for Fang Yanzhi and his kin.
description: A House Fane antagonist during the Trial of Blood (Eps 41-46). Enraged that Zane eliminated his nephew Blake (source: Fang Yanzhi's nephew Zhen'er), he uses a communication slab to feed Zane's location to Joe, the trial's strongest competitor, and orders him to 'make this right'.

name: Blake
issues: Name collision: the 'Blake' of Ep 42 is Chris Fane's nephew eliminated in the Trial of Blood (source: Zhen'er of the Fang family), a different character from the Eps 488-489 Blake, the Cloud Hall Thunder-Law disciple (source: Zong Mo Xie). The two should not be merged.
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name; 'Blake' stands for Zong Mo Xie, the famed Cloud Hall leader who duels the Ethereal Spirit Sect's thunder prodigy at the conference.
description: A Cloud Hall disciple at the Inner-Core Realm who has mastered the Thunder Law (per MasterLS), matched against Edgar of the Ethereal Spirit Sect in the conference duels (Eps 488-489; source: Zong Mo Xie vs. Situ Haoran of the Void Spirit Sect). He leaves the arena battered and is helped back to the Cloud Hall group.

name: Blake and Paxton
reason: Conjunction fragment naming two separate characters (Blake and Paxton), not an entity in its own right.

name: Cyclone Ring
reason: The source's thrown ring weapons, the 'Sky Splitting Rings' feared for their cutting power (Ch ~70), were renamed 'Cyclone Rings' for the adaptation.
description: Thrown ring weapons deployed in the arena duel of Eps 83-84; seven of them can be redirected mid-flight with a flick of the wrist to swarm an opponent from behind, forcing Zane into impossible dodges.

name: Clearhaven
reason: The source city 'Huatian City' in the Upper Realm arc was renamed 'Clearhaven' to fit the Western fantasy register of the adaptation.
description: A city in the Upper Realm arc (Eps 1117-1121) ruled by a lord in a blood-red robe; dozens of other city lords come rushing toward it as events there escalate.

name: Master Sloan
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name: the source's Temple/Palace Master Shen of the tenth-grade Holy Land became 'Master Sloan' ('a hall leader in a tenth-tier sacred place', Ep 1121, mirrors the source line nearly verbatim).
description: A shrewd hall leader of the tenth-tier Lingwu sacred place. Alongside Master Hill (source: Palace Lord He) he oversees Zane during the mine arc (Eps 1024-1028), and later probes Zane's mysterious history over the feast, catching references like the 'Thirteen Palaces' (Eps 1121-1122).
